Prepare the film and community-account activities

Adult: supply an actual suitable short film scene before asking about its words and visible communication clues. For First Nations Australian communication, choose an actual named community-endorsed account with local guidance, identify its community and speaker and use only the explanation it provides. Discuss how those words, symbols or gestures work in that specific account; do not invent a universal sign. These source-specific activities require the supplied source.

Books supplied for the preference try

Use these complete descriptions: Book A has funny animal stories. Book B shows steps for making a kite. Choose either and explain a relevant preference. Alternatively an adult supplies two actual familiar books and lets the learner inspect them before choosing.

The two complete texts for this comparison

Garden recount: “On Monday our class went to the garden. First we looked at the beds. Next we watered them. Last we went back inside.” Report: “Tools: We use a trowel and a watering can. Jobs: We dig small holes and water the beds.” Compare the recount’s time order with the report’s grouped facts.

Contents and screen rules for this check

Print contents: Tools — page 2; Watering — page 4; Growing — page 6. Check each destination’s heading. Model screen: Menu opens the section list; selecting Watering opens that section. The target is Watering: turn to page 4 in print; select Menu then Watering on the model screen. A paper response explains the model, not actual device use.

Prepare the cultural-account activity

Adult: open the named museum resource, read its cultural notices and attribution, and supply the actual artwork, digital flip book and relevant teacher explanation before discussion. Ask what is visibly shown and what the artist’s published account adds. Do not guess the meaning of a cultural symbol or reproduce the artwork. If the actual resource is unavailable, defer its source-specific questions.

An actual map for the tracing task

Adult: before the task, draw and label a school gate, hall and garden on paper. Draw a continuous path from gate past hall to garden, with an arrow showing that direction. Place the actual map beside these words and ask the learner to trace the route. The drawing is a prepared teaching material; this text is not itself a map.

section: See the idea: Link a topic word to its meaning
html:
Meaning supplied for the fresh word

Shelter is a place that helps protect an animal, for example from weather. Use this taught meaning before asking for a sentence. “The rabbit needs a safe shelter” is one possible accurate use.
